subsections.title: Placing Units In Strategic Reserves
text: Before the battle, in the Declare Battle Formations step, you can select one or more friendly units (excluding FORTIFICATIONS) to place in strategic reserves. Instead of setting up these units on the battlefield during deployment, place them to one side; they are strategic reserves units, and will arrive later in the battle.

Unless otherwise stated, the combined points value of all of your strategic reserves units (including those embarked within TRANSPORTS that are themselves placed in strategic reserves) cannot exceed 50% of your points limit for your battle size.

accordions.title: Reserves
text: The term 'Reserves' is the same as strategic reserves.

accordions.title: Strategic Reserves at the End of the Battle
text: At the end of the final turn, units in strategic reserves are destroyed, but they do not trigger rules that apply when a model is destroyed.

subsections.title: Repositioned Units
text: Some rules allow units to be removed from the battlefield and placed in strategic reserves during the battle. Units that use such rules are known as repositioned units. In addition to any other rules that apply to such units (such as where they can or cannot arrive), all of the following rules apply to them:
• If used in the Movement phase, such rules can be used on units that have already moved that phase.
• A repositioned unit that is set up in the same turn in which it made an advance, fall-back or disembark move has still made an advance, fall-back or disembark move that turn.

• When they are removed from the battlefield, any rules that are affecting such units for a specified duration or under specified circumstances continue to affect them while that duration and/or those circumstances apply.

Example: A unit that was within range of an aura ability when removed from the battlefield would no longer be affected by that aura ability if it is no longer within range of it when it makes an ingress move, but a unit that was battle-shocked when removed from the battlefield would still be battle-shocked if it makes an ingress move in the same turn.

subsections.title: Arriving From Strategic Reserves
text: To arrive on the battlefield, each strategic reserves unit must make an ingress move (20.04). Unless otherwise stated, they can only do so from the second battle round onwards.
At the end of the third battle round, unless otherwise stated, all strategic reserves units that have not made one or more ingress moves are destroyed, with the following exceptions:
• Units embarked within TRANSPORTS that have made an ingress move during the battle.
• Repositioned units (20.02).

accordions.title: Set Up As Reinforcements
text: If a rule mentions a unit being set up on the battlefield as Reinforcements, it means a unit that made an ingress move.

subsections.title: Ingress Move
text: Eligible If
Your unit is in strategic reserves (excluding units that are embarked within TRANSPORTS that are themselves in strategic reserves)
Set-up Distance
While Moving
Set up your unit wholly within the set-up distance of one or more battlefield edges and more than 8" horizontally from all enemy units.
• Before the Third Battle Round: While doing so, no models can be set up within your opponent’s deployment zone.
Effect
Your unit is set up as described in Set Up (03.02)
After Moving
Unless otherwise stated, until the start of the next Charge phase, your unit is not eligible to make any other type of move.

faq_screen.question: Aerialists ability allows you to get into a transport even though they disembarked a transport this turn?
faq_screen.answer: Yes, as the unit embarking is not making a normal, advance or fall-back move as part of this embarkation.
faq_screen.reason: Screened: owned by Section18; no new Strategic Reserves exception. Transport embark occasion belongs to Section18; attachment does not grant a new embark occasion.

faq_screen.question: Can I select a unit to shoot or fight if it doesn't have melee or ranged weapons?
faq_screen.answer: Yes, it just makes no attacks and then the fight type or shoot type is resolved.
faq_screen.reason: Screened: owned by Section10/12; no new Strategic Reserves exception. Weaponless activation is owned by Sections10/12; public attached activation is tested without inventing attacks.

faq_screen.question: Can a model be within range of a weapon if it is not visible

faq_screen.reason: Screened: owned by Section04; no new Strategic Reserves exception. Visibility/range independence is Section04; no attached-only exception.

faq_screen.question: How many mortals do you take from Hazardous tests for a combined vehicle/monster and Infantry unit
faq_screen.answer: The roll would be all at once and it would be 1 MW per fail
faq_screen.reason: Screened: owned by Section06; no new Strategic Reserves exception. Mixed-unit Hazard amount is Section06; components do not change the owning hazard rule.

faq_screen.question: I failed hazard rolls from [Hazardous] weapons, do those mortal wounds have to be allocated to the models with the [Hazardous] weapons?
faq_screen.answer: No, you allocate the mortal wounds to the unit as per Mortal Wounds(06.02). (This represents Bob the guardsmen picking up his fallen squad mates plasma gun or that the twisting power of James the Chaos Sorcerer pulling his followers into the warp.)
faq_screen.reason: Screened: owned by Section06; no new Strategic Reserves exception. Mortal allocation/weapon ownership is Section06; attachment introduces no Hazardous bearer lock.

faq_screen.question: I have a rule that triggers when a mortal wound is allocated to a model, when does this happen?
faq_screen.answer: When you select a model in the Select Model step of Mortal Wounds (06.02).
faq_screen.reason: Screened: owned by Section06; no new Strategic Reserves exception. Mortal Select Model timing is Section06; no new Section19 timing rule.

faq_screen.question: I have a unit being attacked with weapons that will modify some of their save rolls to be worse then 6 should I make those save rolls?
faq_screen.answer: Yes, because other models in your unit may have Sv's that are better those models you've mentioned, this means that enough save rolls could be allocated to the those models that the rest of the results are not greater then the Sv's of the other models in your unit.
faq_screen.reason: Screened: owned by Section05; no new Strategic Reserves exception. Heterogeneous Save allocation is shared Section05; highest-T distinction is locally asserted.

faq_screen.question: If I have a rule that says my unit can move up to 6" when it makes a pile-in move or consolidation move, does this also mean it changes the maximum distance of those moves to 6"?
faq_screen.answer: Yes
faq_screen.reason: Screened: owned by Section12; no new Strategic Reserves exception. Pile-in/consolidation maximum is Section12, not changed by attachment.

faq_screen.reason: Screened: owned by Section12; no new Strategic Reserves exception. Fight step-specific movement grant remains Section12.

faq_screen.question: Do a unit's abilities continue to function while they are embarked within a TRANSPORT?
faq_screen.answer: Yes, within the restrictions specified by the ability itself. Embarked units are Not On The Battlefield (01.02.04), so any ability requiring visibility or measurement to another unit will fail. Example: Azrael is attached to an Intercessor Squad unit and embarked within a TRANSPORT, and that TRANSPORT is making a shooting attack using the Firing Deck ability. While Azrael's Supreme Grand Master ability is still technically active, it will have no effect, as the requirements of the ability are not met (the ability affects 'weapons equipped by models' in Azrael's unit, and for the purposes of Firing Deck, the TRANSPORT itself is equipped with those weapons instead).
faq_screen.reason: Screened: owned by Section18; no new Strategic Reserves exception. Direct inherited boundary: embarked abilities and borrowed weapons preserve physical ownership; execute shared Firing Deck consumer.

faq_screen.question: How do modifiers to the charge roll (or to the maximum distance of the charge move, such as Take to the Skies) affect the selection of charge targets?
faq_screen.answer: A charging unit may only select charge targets that are within the maximum distance of their charge roll, including any modifiers. If such a modifier occurs after selecting a charge target and causes that charge target to no longer be within the maximum distance, the charging unit would then select new targets (Target No Longer Eligible Or Viable, 04.03.03). Example: A unit's charge roll is 7", and that unit has a datasheet ability which adds 1 to charge rolls: that charge's maximum distance is 8", so you can select charge targets within 8". Example: A FLYING unit chooses to take to the skies and rolls a charge roll of 9"; that charge's maximum distance is 7" (9" minus the 2" from taking to the skies), so you can select charge targets within 7".
faq_screen.reason: Screened: owned by Section11; no new Strategic Reserves exception. Charge maximum and target reselection remain Section11.
